subject: DeltaThera capacity gap analysis: tokens/sec -> SLO fit
messages:
From: Eleanor Park <eleanor@delta-thera.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Throughput needs for UAT + SLOs

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the demo this week — DeltaThera's engineering team liked the latency profile. We need a concrete sizing estimate for our UAT -> GA ramp so procurement can scope the committed capacity. Key inputs from our side: 
- Target p95 latency for inference: 300 ms (tail-sensitive UI)
- Typical request size: ~150 tokens (mean), stdev ~40
- Concurrent steady-state RPS for UAT: 120 req/s; expected peak multiplier: 3x for short bursts (marketing demos)
- Preferred model: clinically-tuned 13B (we want accuracy parity with our pilot)

Can you provide tokens/sec capacity estimates, GPUs recommended for committed slabs, and suggested headroom for availability/burst? Also include any quick mitigations if the latency SLO is at risk (smaller model, batching limits, prefix cache).

Appreciate a short write-up we can attach to the purchase order.

Best,
Eleanor
Procurement Lead, Delta Therapeutics

From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Eleanor Park <eleanor@delta-thera.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-28T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput needs for UAT + SLOs

Hi Eleanor — thanks, this is helpful. Below is our initial, conservative sizing + mitigation plan. I've cc'd Ben (AE) and Laura (Capacity) to validate assumptions and final numbers.

Summary (short):
- Sustained tokens/sec demand (steady state) = 120 req/s * 150 tokens = 18,000 tokens/sec
- Peak burst demand (3x) = 54,000 tokens/sec
- Baseline model option: clinical-13B quantized (accuracy target). Measured single-GPU median throughput ~360 tokens/sec for our quantized 13B serving profile with typical 8k context and low output length variance.
- GPUs required (baseline math):
  - Steady: 18,000 / 360 ≈ 50 GPUs
  - Peak (no autoscale): 54,000 / 360 ≈ 150 GPUs
- Recommended committed slab: 60 GPUs reserved (≈20% steady headroom) + autoscale burst pool for peak. Rationale: reservation keeps steady costs predictable and provides buffer for background variance; autoscale covers marketing/demo spikes.

Latency risk and mitigations:
1) With baseline config and sustained load at 50 GPUs, median latency is within target, but p95 can drift if KV cache miss rate is high or if batch sizes grow.
2) To protect p95 at 300 ms:
   - Enforce per-request batching cap (max batch size 8). This bounds queuing latency.
   - Enable prefix/KV cache for repeated prompts (expected to reduce work by ~15–25% for our UI patterns).
   - Canary a quantized-7B clinical-tuned variant (single-GPU throughput ~760 tokens/sec) for non-critical traffic: reduces reserved GPUs needed.

Alternative (cost-optimized) option:
- Use clinical-7B quantized for 80% of traffic, 13B for high-risk calls -> effective tokens/sec per reserved GPU ~620 (weighted), reducing steady slab to ~30–35 GPUs. Tradeoff: small quality delta on edge cases.

Next steps:
1) Ben / Laura: can you confirm the single-GPU throughput assumptions (360 tps for 13B q, 760 tps for 7B q) and add any operational constraints for autoscale?
2) Eleanor: if you can share a 48-hour sample request trace (anonymized), we can run a quick sim that will refine the p95 projection and the recommended slab size.

Attachments: delta_20280728_sizing_sheet.xlsx (spreadsheet with per-model sims)

Thanks — I can turn this into a one-page sizing appendix for procurement once Ben/Lauren validate.

— Olga
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, Eleanor Park <eleanor@delta-thera.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-28T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput needs for UAT + SLOs

Thanks Olga — validating numbers and adding an ops-minded option. I re-ran quick sims with our 7B/13B kernels and realistic batch distributions (mix of 1–6). Key callouts:

Measured single-GPU (production kernels):
- clinical-13B (q4x) -> median sustained 360 tokens/sec; p95 throughput lower when tail queries use >512 tokens output.
- clinical-7B (q4x) -> median sustained 780 tokens/sec
Sizing scenarios (rounded):
A) Accuracy-first (13B everywhere):
  - Steady tokens/sec: 18k -> ~50 GPUs required
  - Reserve recommendation: 60 GPUs (20% headroom), autoscale bucket configured to add up to +120 GPUs for 3x bursts (pre-warmed slabs can be scheduled during known demo windows)
B) Hybrid (7B fallback for non-critical requests):
  - Weighted effective per-GPU: ~620 tps -> steady slab ~29 GPUs -> recommend 36 GPUs reserved (20% headroom) + burst pool
C) Aggressive cost scenario (13B for <20% of calls):
  - Steady slab ~20 GPUs but higher risk to p95; not recommended for your interactive UI.

Operational guardrails:
- Autoscale cold-start: allow pre-warming window for demo days (we can stage pre-warmed GPUs 15 minutes before peak).
- Canary rollout: start hybrid with 10% traffic on 7B for two days, monitor quality metrics and token savings.

I've uploaded a short sim (p95_latency_sim_report.pdf) with the p95 prob distributions across the scenarios. If you want, we can include the canary plan and cost delta in the PO appendix.
— Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Eleanor Park <eleanor@delta-thera.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-29T14:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput needs for UAT + SLOs

Hi all — this is exactly what procurement needs, thank you. A few quick notes:
- We'll share an anonymized 48-hour trace tomorrow (Matt will upload).
- Procurement preference is to avoid large autoscale charges; they asked for two formal options in the PO appendix: (1) Accuracy-first (60 GPU reserved + burst) and (2) Hybrid cost-optimized (36 GPU reserved + burst).
- Can you include a short bullet on expected monthly $ delta between the two (ballpark)? We have an internal cap for the first contract term.

If you can turn the two scenarios into a 1–2 page appendix with the sim attachments and a recommended roll-forward plan (canary steps + pre-warm schedule), we'll attach it to the purchase order and start the legal cycle.

Thanks,
Eleanor
Procurement Lead, Delta Therapeutics
